name: Operation Midnight Cipher
description:
Scenario Overview

The SOC receives a cascade of alerts that, when correlated, reveal a coordinated campaign against a regional bank. The adversary starts with open‑source reconnaissance of the target’s public IP ranges (T1590) and searches technical databases for exposed employee emails (T1596). Using underground marketplaces, they acquire a custom PowerShell dropper (T1585) and a legitimate remote‑access tool (T1588). The dropper is delivered via a spearphishing attachment (T1566.001) and executes a PowerShell script (T1059.001) that injects into LSASS (T1055) to harvest credentials (T1110, T1539). The malware enumerates system information (T1082) and domain accounts (T1673) before establishing C2 over a disguised web service (T1102) and leveraging the remote‑access tool (T1219). Finally, the threat actor disables backups (T1490) and defaces the public portal (T1491) to maximize impact.

Your Mission

  • Investigate the initial phishing attachment that delivered the PowerShell dropper.
  • Identify the process‑injection technique used to capture credentials.
  • Correlate the stealthy C2 traffic hidden in legitimate web service calls.
  • Map the discovery steps that revealed system and account information.
  • Develop containment and remediation steps to stop credential theft, restore backups, and remove defacement.
